IN THE SUPREME COURT OF INDIA
CIVIL APPELLATE JURISDICTION
CIVIL APPEAL NO.10611/2026
(@Petition for Special Leave to Appeal (C) No.19710/2026)
JABBAR KHAN                                        Appellant(s)
                                VERSUS
GOHAR ALAM & ORS.                                  Respondent(s)
 O R D E R
1. Exemption Applications are allowed.
2. Leave granted.
3. This appeal challenges the impugned Order which is said to
have been disposed of on first date of hearing without even issuing
notice to the Respondents. Respondent Nos.1 and 3 are represented
herein by Ms. Puja Sharma, the learned counsel but Respondent No.2
has not yet been served. The contesting parties are the Appellant
and the 1st Respondent - herein.
4. The 1st Respondent is said to have purchased the property from
Respondent Nos.2 and 3 and was the plaintiff in the Suit. The Trial
Court dismissed the Suit. The Appellant - herein was Defendant No.1
who claimed tenancy in the property from 1991. The High Court,
considering the appeal from the dismissal of the Suit, reversed it
without issuing notice to the 1st Respondent, who is the Appellant -
herein.
5. We see that Respondents before the High Court were not
represented and we do not see any recital in the Judgment as to the
notice having been issued to them, nor they having been declared

## Page 459

2
ex-parte by reason of not recording their presence, despite receipt
of notice. 
6. We, hence, set aside the impugned Order of the High Court, but
without any observations on the merits.
7. We direct that the Appeal stands restored to the High Court
and be considered afresh after hearing both the parties.
8. The Appeal stands disposed of.
9. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.

       UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. At this point in time, we are dealing with two specific
issues:
(i) The accused involved in  NDPS cases, especially
foreign nationals who have jumped the bail and are now
not traceable.
(ii) What is the mechanism in place and what steps have
been  taken  by  the  Governments  of  Punjab,  Himachal
Pradesh and Haryana and ensuring their arrest and/or
securing their presence for trial. 
2

application for suspension of sentence and bail.

involvement in the murder of Sunil Namdev, wherein the appellant

deceased and the injuries sustained turned fatal. The appellant is
alleged to have held the hands of the victim when the others struck

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following

1. We have heard learned counsel for the parties.
2. Leave granted.
3. Appellant(s) have been convicted by the Trial
Court under Section 306 r/w Section 34 of the Indian
1

## Page 492

Penal Code, 1860 (for short, ‘IPC’) and sentenced to
undergo Rigorous Imprisonment (for short, ‘R.I.’) for
05 years with a default stipulation. The conviction and
sentence has been affirmed by the High Court.
4. Insofar appellant(s) are concerned, we find that
Appellant No.1 is the step mother of the informant
whereas Appellant No.2 is the step sister of the
informant. Appellant No.1 is almost 80 years of age
whereas Appellant No.2 is of 40 years of age.
5. It is a case of death by committing suicide.
Suicide has been committed by consuming insecticide.
6. Case of the defence is that the bottle in which
the insecticide was kept was not sent to the Forensic
Science Laboratory for examination. That apart, no
expert opinion was obtained regarding the nature of the
insecticide. The seizure witness, P.W.6, only witnessed
seizure of the bottle.
7. This aspect of the matter has not been considered
by the High Court.
8. Prima facie, we are of the view that a case for
suspension of sentence and bail is made out, pending
disposal of the appeal.
9. Consequently, we suspend the sentence and direct
that the appellant(s) shall be produced before the
concerned Sessions Court within a maximum period of 07
days from today, whereafter they shall be released on
bail on such terms and conditions as may be deemed
2

appropriate.
10. List  the  Criminal  Appeal  for  hearing  in  due
course.

submits that as the tenure of elected Society Member of
the  Shivayogi Swamy Memorial Education Society (for
short, ‘the Society’) has come to an end and as fresh
elections have taken place during the pendency of the
instant petition, nothing survives for consideration by
this Court in this petition. However, he urges that the
observations made in the impugned order may not be
treated as prejudicial to the cause of any of the
contesting parties in the future election process.
4. Mr. Shivalinga Swamy, the respondent appearing-
in-person, on the other hand, submits that he has been
declared as the President of the Society and the result
has been filed before the Registrar. 
5. We are of the opinion that there is no occasion
for this Court to adjudicate upon the claim of the
respondent-in-person that he has been elected to be the
President of the Society. Since the petitioner has
stated before this Court that the matter has become
infructuous, the special leave petition is disposed of
as  infructuous  while  making  it  clear  that  the
observations made in the impugned judgment shall not

the parties.
The limited grievance of the appellant(s) is
that on the very first date of hearing the matter,
the impugned order has been passed by the High Court
without facilitating the appellant to bring certain
factual aspects on record.
On a perusal of the impugned order, we find that
the statement made at the bar by the learned counsel
appearing for the appellant is correct.
In such view of the matter, we set aside the
impugned order by remitting the matter to the High
Court for fresh consideration, after affording an
opportunity of being heard to both the sides.
Both  sides  are  at  liberty  to  file  the
appropriate affidavits, along with the documents,
within a period of six weeks from the date of
receipt of a copy of this order.

1. Leave granted.

present appeal, being aggrieved by the impugned final
judgment dated  24.09.2020 passed by the High Court of
Himachal Pradesh at Shimla in Criminal Appeal No.408 of
2019, whereby the conviction and sentence of 11 years’
rigorous imprisonment imposed upon the appellant under
Section 20(b)(ii)(C) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic
Substances  Act,  1985,  by  the  Special  Judge,  Chamba
Division, Chamba, Himachal Pradesh, in Sessions Trial No.
15 of 2017, was affirmed.
3. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the appellant
has argued before this Court that the appellant has been
falsely implicated, and if the evidence is taken into
consideration, there is every likelihood of his acquittal.
He has also argued that the appellant has undergone 09
years of sentence out of 11 years sentence awarded to him. 
4. On  the  other  hand,  learned  counsel  for  the
respondent-State has vehemently opposed the prayer for
suspension of sentence. 
5. This Court, after hearing the learned counsel for
the parties and keeping in view the grounds raised on
behalf of the appellant, is of the opinion that learned
counsel for the appellant has been able to make out a case
for suspension of sentence, and, therefore, the prayer for
suspension of sentence deserves to be allowed. Accordingly,
2

## Page 526

the prayer is allowed.
6. The appellant is accordingly directed to be released
on bail during the pendency of the appeal, subject to such
terms and conditions as may be imposed by the Trial Court.
7. List the appeal for final hearing in due course.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The instant petition has been filed for grant of regular bail
in  RC-14/2021/NIA/DLI  registered  at  Police  Station  NIA  under
Sections 124A, 153A, 153B of the IPC and Sections 17, 18, 38, 39
and 40 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.  It seems
that there were a total of 12 accused persons, out of whom 4 are
absconding. It is stated that after completing the investigation, a
chargesheet was filed against the remaining 8 accused persons,
including the petitioner.  
2. When this matter came up for hearing, this Court expanded the
scope of this petition and passed various orders from time to time.
Pursuant thereto, the Union of India has now established Special
Courts for the exclusive trial of cases under NIA. The petitioner’s
case has also been transferred to one of such Special Courts where
charges have also been framed.  
2

## Page 538

3. In such circumstances, while we are not inclined to enlarge the
petition on bail at this stage, we dispose of this petition with a
direction to the learned Special Court to examine the vital and
protracted witnesses within a period of six months and ensure that
the entire trial is concluded within a period of one year.  For
this purpose, the case shall be taken up on a day-to-day basis, if
so required.
4. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand closed.

       UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The petitioner and the complainant are related to
each other inasmuch as petitioner’s daughter is
married to complainant’s son.  The allegation is
1

## Page 616

that the petitioner jumped over the gate with a
chopper assaulting the complainant resulting in some
injuries.  The incident is of the year 2011 and by
now 15 years have passed.  It is the case of the
petitioner that the complainant is no more alive and
thereafter his son is impleaded to represent the
complainant.  Besides, the petitioner’s daughter and
the complainant’s son have since separated.  In such
circumstances, it is the submission of the learned
counsel for the petitioner that to secure the ends
of  justice  it  would  be  appropriate  that  these
proceedings which were initiated on account of sour
relationship  between  petitioner’s  daughter  and
complainant’s son be closed particularly when there
is no likelihood of any conviction inasmuch as the
complainant who has been the witness of the incident
is no more alive. Besides, the injuries found during
medical examination are simple in nature.
2. Delay condoned.
3. Issue notice, returnable in eight weeks.
4. In the meantime, further proceedings emanating from
FIR  No.621  of  2011  registered  at  P.S.  Pettah,
District Thruvananthapuram shall remain stayed.
      (KAVITA PAHUJA)                              (SAPNA BANSAL)

Date : 10-08-2026 This matter was called on for hearing today.
CORAM :  HON'BLE THE CHIEF JUSTICE
         HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE JOYMALYA BAGCHI
         HON'BLE MRS. JUSTICE V. MOHANA
For Petitioner(s) :  Petitioner-in-person
                    
For Respondent(s) : 
          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Permission to appear and argue in-person is granted.
2. Delay condoned.
3. We have heard the petitioner in-person at a considerable
length.
4. While we do not find any ground to interfere with the impugned
judgment of the High Court declining to entertain a Public Interest
Litigation  on  behalf  of  the  petitioner  for  enforcement  of
individual rights of her 33 co-villagers re: the grant of patta
rights, we do appreciate the initiative taken by the petitioner for
enforcement of the perceived legal rights of her village community.
1

## Page 798

5. In this regard, we have impressed upon the petitioner to take
the co-villagers to the office of the District Legal Services
Authority and ensure that legal aid counsel are engaged on behalf
of  every  individual  villager.  Since  the  petitioner  is  well-
conversant with the facts of the individual cases, she can assist
greatly in drafting the claim petitions. The petitioner, in our
opinion, will be better than any para-legal volunteer for this
purpose, and it will be highly appreciated if she renders her
services in ensuring that the claims of similarly placed claimants
are timely settled/decided by the competent authority in accordance
with law. 
6. It goes without saying that if the need arises, the legal aid
counsel will be provided to the eligible claimants for pursuing
their remedy before the High Court or any other authority, and for
such proceedings, the petitioner may also assist the legal aid
counsel or the parties seeking enforcement of their rights. 
7. It is needless to mention that in case claimants that are
similarly placed as the petitioner approach the Forest Authorities,
their  claim  application  shall  be  decided  at  the  earliest,
preferably within one month from the date of submission of such
application(s).
8. The Special Leave Petitions are, accordingly, disposed of.
9. All pending applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. In deference to our order dated 03.08.2026, the learned
Solicitor General of India has placed on record an exhaustive Brief
Note-cum-Action Taken Report that highlights the efforts made by
the Indian Embassies in Ukraine and Romania as well as the
initiatives undertaken by the Ministry of External Affairs to
confirm the whereabouts of the missing persons. The report points
out that between 31.07.2026 and 05.08.2026, the Directorate General
of Maritime Administration (DGMA) continuously followed up with all
1

## Page 802

concerned  stakeholders,  embassy  channels,  and  governmental
authorities seeking updated Search and Rescue (SAR) status, crew
welfare information, flag-State investigation findings, Protection
and Indemnity reports, and final SAR documentation. He explained
that on 04.08.2026 and 05.08.2026, the DGMA received further
updates through vessel management confirming that Romanian Maritime
Rescue Coordination Centre (MRCC) had not located the missing crew
members despite exhaustive SAR efforts and that operations remained
suspended pending fresh information. The status report further
highlights  the  compliance  with  International  Maritime
Organization/International Labour Organization Guidelines on Fair
Treatment of Seafarers. 
2. It is pointed out that as per the information received upto
05.08.2026,  extensive  SAR  operations  undertaken  by  Ukrainian
Authorities, Romanian MRCC, Romanian Coast Guard, and associated
rescue services were unable to locate Mr. Deepak Kumar Gupta and
Mr.  Ram  Chandra  Dubey.  It  is  stated  that  search  operations
presently remain suspended pending receipt of fresh information,
while the DGMA continues to pursue all pending investigation/SAR
reports and remains engaged with all concerned stakeholders.
3. Post for further consideration on 31.08.2026.
4. Meanwhile, a fresh status report be filed to apprise this
Court of further updates.

          UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. Mr. Shailesh Madiyal, learned senior counsel appearing for the appellants
has  placed  before  us  a  chart indicating  the  status  of the  appellants  up  to
August, 2026.
2. We find that some of the appellants were promoted as Audit Officers in
the year 2017, although, while granting leave on the special leave petitions
from  which  the  present  appeals  arise,  this  Court  by  its  order  dated  28th
November, 2016 had directed status quo as on that date to be maintained.
3. We  are  surprised  as  to  how  the  State  of  Assam  could  have  granted
promotion to some of the appellants during the subsistence of such interim
order.
4. Learned counsel appearing for the State of Assam seeks and is granted
three weeks’ time to file an affidavit and explain that there has been no breach
of this Court’s order dated 28th November, 2016.
5. Relist the appeals after four weeks.

For Petitioner(s) :Mr. Hitendra Nath Rath, AOR
                   Ms. Laxmi, Adv.                   
                   
For Respondent(s) : 
           UPON hearing the counsel the Court made the following
                             O R D E R
1. The  only  ground  taken  in  this  Transfer  Petition  is  of
inconvenience, which as per the decision in ”M/s. Shri Sendhur Agro
& Oil Industries vs. Kotak Mahindra Bank Ltd. in TP (Crl.) No.
608/2024 reported in 2025 INSC 328” , cannot be raised successfully
for praying for transfer of a particular case, especially, criminal
case under Section 406 Cr.P.C. and Section 446 B.N.S.S.
2. In view of the above, and in view of the fact that no other
ground is raised except inconvenience, the present petition stands
dismissed.
3. Accordingly, the Transfer Petition stands dismissed.
4. Pending application(s), if any, shall stand disposed of.
